name: Metallurgical accounting (daily mill balance and month-end true-up)
summary: Every day the mill metallurgist turns the shift logs, belt-scale and historian data and the assay results for the shift composite samples into a balance of tonnes milled, head grade, tailings grade, recovery and gold produced, and issues a daily production report to the mill superintendent and the general manager. Once a month the balance is closed: the mill samples gold held in tanks and solution, the gold room cleans up and pours, the metallurgist calculates gold in circuit and then trues up produced ounces to the refinery's outturn for the month's shipments before the numbers go to site finance, technical services and head office. The work is slow and error-prone because process assays come back a day or two later from the company laboratory in Wawa, the belt scale drifts, and everything is re-keyed by hand into a workbook.

baseline.org_archetype: A 300-person single-mine Ontario gold producer with a 1,000-1,200 t/d Merrill-Crowe mill 17 km from the mine, a company assay office in Wawa and one or two metallurgists on 14/14 rotation.
baseline.notes: Modelled on a single-mine northern Ontario gold producer (Eagle River mine and mill near Wawa) as described in the organisation file; site practice from the Eagle River technical reports where they say it.

unit_of_work: one daily balance (one production day, 07:00 to 07:00; about one in thirty also closes the month)
trigger: The night shift supervisor closes the shift log at the end of the production day.
end_state: The daily production report is issued and accepted by the mill superintendent; on the last day of the month the monthly metallurgical balance, adjusted to refinery outturn, is signed off and sent to site finance, technical services and head office.

volume.seasonality: One balance every day of the year; the month-end close adds one heavy day of work and a wait for refinery outturns.

evidence.note: The mill runs continuously (srk2022) and the site metallurgist prepares daily and monthly metallurgical reports and manages mill month-end reporting (wdometjob, 2024 posting). Count of one balance per calendar day follows from that.

Organisation file role (2 people). Two metallurgists cover the 14/14 rotation, so one is on site; daily balance work takes about 2.5 hours a day plus two to three days at month end, about half of one on-site metallurgist. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

Organisation file role (1 people). Reviews the daily report each morning and signs the monthly balance. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

Organisation file role (4 people). Each 12-hour shift supervisor closes the shift log; two shifts a day. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

roles.title: Mill process and control room operator

evidence.note: Organisation file role (16 people). Operators cut and bag shift composite samples and take the month-end circuit inventory samples. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.
Organisation file role (2 people). Month-end clean-up pour and bar weights. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

systems.name: Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Mill distributed control system and process historian
Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)

resources.name: Refinery (sock burner oven and propane furnace in a secure room)

steps.name: Close shift log
steps.description: At the end of each 12-hour shift the mill shift supervisor completes the shift log: belt-scale tonnes, grind density readings, reagent additions, downtime with causes and the list of composite samples taken. The day and night logs for the production day are both counted here.

error.defect_description: Downtime or reagent figures left blank or copied from the previous shift.

evidence.note: Mill runs 24/7 with two crews on 12-hour shifts (wdo2016). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Cut and bag shift composite samples
steps.description: A mill operator collects the shift composite samples of mill feed, leach discharge, barren solution and filtered tailings, dries or decants them as needed, labels each bag and writes the sample sheet for the daily shuttle to the assay office.

error.defect_description: Mislabelled or swapped sample bags.

evidence.note: Mill samples are assayed at the company assay office in Wawa (wdo2016, srk2022). Sample set and times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Receive process assays from the lab
steps.description: The assay office in Wawa fire-assays the process samples brought by the daily shuttle and the assay supervisor emails the results file to the mill. The metallurgist waits for this file before the balance can be finalised; laboratory work itself is in the fire assay laboratory workflow.

error.defect_description: Wrong sample ID attached to a result.

evidence.note: Samples go to Wawa daily by company shuttle and results are reported by email (wdo2016, srk2022). Turnaround of one to two days: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Pull historian and belt-scale data
steps.description: The metallurgist opens the DCS historian and exports the day's belt-scale tonnage, mill feed rates, cyclone densities, solution flows and zinc and cyanide additions, and checks the belt-scale totaliser against the shift logs for drift or gaps when the scale was down.

error.defect_description: Belt-scale drift or a data gap not corrected.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Key shift log and process data into the workbook
steps.description: The metallurgist types the tonnes, moisture, downtime, reagent use and solution volumes from the two shift logs and the historian export into the daily sheet of the metallurgical accounting workbook, fixing blanks by radio or email with the shift supervisor.

error.defect_description: Transposition or units error when re-keying.

evidence.note: Re-keying into workbooks is common in small mills of the period; Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Load and screen process assays
steps.description: The metallurgist pastes the assay file into the workbook and compares each feed, solution and tailings grade with recent values and with the grade expected from the mine's reported ore. A result that is far out of line, or a missing sample, is sent back to the lab for a re-assay.

error.defect_description: An outlier assay accepted.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Calculate daily balance
steps.description: The metallurgist calculates dry tonnes milled, assayed and back-calculated head grade, tailings losses in solids and solution, recovery and gold produced to gravity concentrate and to the sock presses, and compares head grade with the mine's estimate of the ore delivered.

error.defect_description: Formula broken or moisture not applied.

evidence.note: Check-in check-out balance from measured input and output streams (gaylard2006). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check gold room production against the balance
steps.description: The metallurgist looks up the gold room record for the day's gravity table concentrate and any sock clean-up and compares recovered gold with the balance, carrying the difference as gold in circuit until the month-end clean-up.

error.defect_description: Pour recorded against the wrong day.

evidence.note: Gravity concentrate is upgraded on a shaking table daily and press socks are removed bi-weekly for smelting (srk2022). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Issue daily production report
steps.description: The metallurgist updates the month-to-date sheet and emails the daily production report with tonnes, grades, recovery, ounces and downtime to the mill superintendent, the general manager, the mine superintendent and the chief geologist.

error.defect_description: Report sent with last month's month-to-date range.

evidence.note: Daily metallurgical reports are a stated duty (wdometjob). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review daily report at morning meeting
steps.description: The mill superintendent reads the report before or during the morning production meeting, questions any drop in recovery, odd head grade or belt-scale problem, and either accepts it or sends it back for correction.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

next.condition: last production day of the month

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022. Share of month-end days is 1 in 30.

steps.name: Plan month-end inventory and clean-up
steps.description: The metallurgist agrees with the mill superintendent and shift supervisors the time of the month-end cut-off, which tanks, clarifiers and the zinc precipitate presses will be sampled or cleaned out, and books the gold room for a clean-up pour.

error.defect_description: A tank or press left out of the inventory.

evidence.note: In-process stocks must be verified by physical stocktakes at prescribed intervals (gaylard2006). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Sample circuit inventory
steps.description: Mill operators take slurry and solution samples from each leach tank, thickener, clarifier and solution tank at the cut-off time, record levels and densities, and send the inventory samples to the assay office on the shuttle.

error.defect_description: Unrepresentative sample from a poorly mixed tank.

control.basis: Site cyanide handling procedure and Regulation 854 (mines and mining plants) protection when sampling cyanide tanks

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Clean up presses and pour month-end doré
steps.description: Gold room operators strip the zinc precipitate socks, burn them in the sock oven, smelt the ash and table concentrate in the furnace, pour, weigh and sample the bars and record them under the two-person rule.

error.defect_description: Bar weight or sample mislabelled.

control.basis: Gold room security procedure: two-person rule and camera coverage for all handling of precious metal

evidence.note: Refinery is a restricted-entry room with CCTV, vault, sock burner oven and Wabi furnace; socks and table concentrate smelted to doré of 80-94% gold (srk2022). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Receive inventory and bar assays
steps.description: The assay supervisor emails the assays of the inventory samples and the bar samples after they have been through the Wawa laboratory; the metallurgist cannot close the month without them.

error.defect_description: Bar assay keyed to the wrong bar.

evidence.note: Doré bars are assayed at the company assay office (srk2022). Turnaround: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Calculate gold in circuit and monthly ounces
steps.description: The metallurgist multiplies each tank and solution volume by its assay, adds gold held in socks and in unpoured concentrate, and closes the month: ounces poured plus change in gold in circuit equals ounces produced, compared with ounces from the daily balances.

error.defect_description: Volume or density error in the inventory.

evidence.note: Plant and in-process stock figures verified by stocktake and fed into financial reports (gaylard2006). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Collect stockpile survey and mine tonnage
steps.description: The metallurgist gets the month-end survey of the ore pad and fine ore bin and the hoisted and trucked ore tonnes from technical services, and records opening and closing ore stocks so mined, stockpiled and milled tonnes tie together.

error.defect_description: Survey and belt-scale tonnes differ and are forced to agree.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for refinery outturns
steps.description: Produced ounces are reported on the mine's own bar weights and assays until the refinery issues final outturns for the month's shipments. The metallurgist issues a preliminary month and holds the final close until outturns arrive, usually two to three weeks after the last shipment.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Doré awaiting refining is expected to complete refining within one month (wdofs2021); final metal values are settled from the receiver's weights and assays, with umpire analysis when results differ (lbmavar2017). Wait length: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: True up to refinery outturn
steps.description: The metallurgist compares, bar by bar, the mine's weights and gold assays with the refinery's outturn, calculates the variance, and adjusts produced ounces and gold in circuit so the month reflects refined ounces. A variance beyond the site's tolerance is investigated.

error.defect_description: Outturn matched to the wrong shipment.

evidence.note: Mass, sampling and analysis each add variance between two parties' numbers (lbmavar2017). Share beyond tolerance: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Investigate refinery variance
steps.description: The metallurgist reviews the bar sampling and assay records with the gold room operators and the assay supervisor, checks scale calibration certificates and, if needed, asks the refinery for its sample results or an umpire assay before deciding which figure to book.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Settlement waits for negotiation or umpire analysis when results differ beyond agreed limits (lbmavar2017). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review and sign monthly balance
steps.description: The mill superintendent reviews the monthly metallurgical report, the gold in circuit, the outturn adjustment and the comparison with the mine's reported grade, asks for corrections where needed and signs it.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Internal control over reported production and inventory: independent review of the monthly metal balance (NI 52-109 certification of disclosure controls)

evidence.note: Metal accounting outputs feed the financial reports and need audit trails and independent audit (gaylard2006). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Approve production numbers for head office
steps.description: The general manager reads the signed monthly report alongside the mine and cost reports and approves the produced ounces, tonnes and grade that site finance and head office will use in the monthly report and any production release.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Site delegation of authority: general manager approves reported production

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Distribute monthly production report
steps.description: The metallurgist saves the closed workbook, sends the monthly balance to technical services for the mine-to-mill reconciliation and the production report to the site controller and to head office, and rolls the workbook forward to the new month.

error.defect_description: An older version of the workbook sent.

evidence.note: Manage mill month-end reporting (wdometjob). Times: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Re-assay of a process sample
exceptions.description: A feed or tailings assay far from recent values or a missing sample is sent back to the Wawa lab and the balance waits another day.

exceptions.name: Superintendent query on the daily report
exceptions.description: A drop in recovery or a head grade out of line with the mine's estimate sends the balance back for checking.

exceptions.name: Refinery variance beyond tolerance
exceptions.description: At month end the refinery outturn differs from the mine's bar figures by more than tolerance and the metallurgist investigates sampling, weighing and assays before booking.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from end of production day to accepted daily report (month-end closes take 2 to 4 weeks)
benchmarks.population: Small Ontario gold mill with an off-site assay office

evidence.note: Daily shuttle to the Wawa assay office and email results (wdo2016) put final assays one to two days after the production day; the author's estimate adds the morning review.

benchmarks.unit: percent of contained gold paid by the refiner

evidence.note: Island Gold NSR assumptions: Au payable 99.96%, refining and transport charge 3.25 per oz.

pain_points.description: Process assays travel 1.5 hours by road to the company assay office in Wawa, so the daily balance is final only a day or two after the production day.

evidence.note: Lab in Wawa, samples shuttled daily (srk2022); trip from Wawa takes about 1.5 hours (wdo2016).

pain_points.description: Shift log and historian figures are re-keyed by hand into the met workbook, and a broken formula or units slip carries into reported production.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice in small Ontario gold mills, 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: The month cannot be finally closed until refinery outturns arrive two to three weeks later, so production is reported provisionally and adjusted later.

evidence.note: Gold doré awaiting refining is expected to complete refining within one month of the statement date (wdofs2021).

assumptions: Simulated median cycle time is about 2.1 days against a tier C estimate of 1.8 days for the daily path; month-end closes add two to four weeks and fall beyond the 90th percentile because they are one case in thirty.

The Eagle River mill recovers gold by gravity concentration and Merrill-Crowe zinc precipitation (srk2022), not carbon-in-pulp; the gold room smelts table concentrate and burned press socks. The organisation file's mill-elution-refining description (carbon elution, electrowinning) does not match this, but the elution-circuit resource id is used here for the gold room furnace.

One case is one production day. About one day in thirty is the last day of the month and also runs the month-end close (s11-s22), so the simulated median reflects the daily path and the 90th percentile does not include month-end closes.
The daily balance is final only when process assays return; a preliminary report on belt-scale tonnes is often issued the same morning and is not modelled separately.
Laboratory hands-on time is counted in the fire assay laboratory workflow; s03 and s14 hold only the release of results and the waits.
Staffing check: hands-on time times 30 balances a month implies about 1.0 FTE and the roles state about 1.1 FTE, so the two agree.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.30 for staff, 1.35 for hourly site roles).

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24 to match this workflow's sources: ids were renamed (mill-elution-refining to mill-gold-room-refining, loaded_carbon to gold_concentrate, tailings_slurry to filtered_tailings, elution-circuit to refinery), and roles and resources this workflow added are now in the organisation file. Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.
